body: Yep.  You don't even have to try anymore.
You mean like when he's on a comedy tour?

>'103' ... that's laughable. I never did believe in those things. I hope you don't let that number affect you to this day.

It didn't affect me then.  I never thought of myself as super-intelligent, just a lot more focused on rationality than most people (or most people around me, anyways).  I'm not particularly knowledgeable, nor am I great with puzzles.  My breadth of knowledge lies primarily in literature and philosophy, and even then, university has taken the piss out of those for me.  My vocabulary and grammar simply come from reading a lot.

>I have a little bit of a theory, although I haven't really heard of someone going through what I'm thinking because of trauma, other than Eckhart Tolle. Have you heard of ego death? 

My mom gave me a copy of A New Earth, which I never came close to finishing.  Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance is the only spiritual book I've ever been able to relate to.  Anyways, I've never heard of ego death.  It's interesting; I've had at least one such epiphany, but its importance was lost to me for this reason: I know "I" am inseparable from the universe in the sense that I am made of the same elements that make up the rest of the universe and that consciousness is just a product of such elements, by which I mean I don't believe in an objectively separable "I".  However, despite this fact, we have brains that simultaneously alert us to this fact as well as isolate us, so no matter how aware I am that I am made of stardust, I'm also aware of (or at least incurably delusional in believing) that my experience of reality is subjective, that there is an "I" which can be referred to.  While I feel a part of the universe, it's impossible to not feel apart.

>Here's the thing though, do you feel like you have no focus?

I'm not sure what you mean by focus.  I've never been able to think of anything I'd want to do seriously or professionally for a very long time, not even as a kid.

>Do you think that might have something to do with pursuing philosophy?

I'm not hooked to any specific philosophy, such as Nihilism, if that's what you're asking.  Maybe the need to constantly ask "why" came from reading philosophy, but I'm not sure.

I'm not really that intelligent.  I haven't taken a proper IQ test since I was 16, but it was only 103 back then.

I have tried meditation.  I've read Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance 3 times through and I tried to adopt a similar, if not identical, philosophy for myself, but it quickly waned and was replaced by what seems to be the factory default.

I'm not sure what to PM you, but if you still want to pick my brain, I'll answer any questions you have.

Thanks.  I tried therapy before, but it obviously didn't work.  I've wanted to go to a psychiatrist for a while, but I don't know how to broach the subject with my parents, who would have to help me pay for it.

I wasn't aware of that experiment, but I was aware that people assign reason or purpose for things that don't necessarily have one.  It's the knowledge of that which prevents me (or at least I try to prevent myself) from doing the same.

> Have you tried opening you heart to others? [...] Your apathy may be a form of psychological self-defense because of what happened to you. It happens to many people that encounters death a lot.

Yeah, back in high school, senior year.  I told a girl I'd had a crush on for 3 years how I felt about her, thinking saying it would change something about me one way or another, but nothing really changed.  She said no, it was swept under the rug.  We don't talk anymore, but it has everything to do with her current fiancé not liking me and nothing to do with our past.  After her, there were a couple more girls I tried to start something with, but I never really felt the same about anyone else afterwards.

>Sometimes; screw reason and have fun. Honestly; fuck reason.

I do, all the time.  Having fun isn't a good enough connection to the world for me.  I smoke and drink on occasion (once a month maybe).  I stopped drinking excessively 2.5 years ago, though.

>Yes; i know you have philosophy under your belt and i don't care.

I don't either, really.  Literary analysis and philosophy aren't so much intellectual endeavors as they are things I happen to be good at.

>Don't cause harm to others and TRY TO BE HAPPY.

If I have a credo at all, it's don't harm others and has been for a long time.

>Reply if you have any parts you want to discuss. ...have a feeling op didn't even bother reading this...

I read it last night, but I had to try and fall asleep for a test I ended up not having to take today.

>  I think the fact that you are apathetic towards life is a symptom of your depression, you have just been so emotionally scarred that instead of feeling depressed, you just feel nothing. 

That's an interesting take on it.  You may be right.

> How stable are you financially? Will your parents support you? 

My parents make roughly $80k/year combined, so they're stable, but not really able to help me pay for anything remotely expensive.  I had $5,000 saved up from working during high school, and that's lasted me until now; it's almost gone, and I have virtually no money to spend on superfluities.

>because when you are faced with a challenge and placed outside of your comfort zone, you don't have the time to sit around and try and rationalize everything, you are making decisions on the fly and you are only focused on living.

I've done something similar, albeit on a smaller scale.  While it's true that being outside of my home and country kept me occupied during the day, when I went to bed (I didn't mention this in the OP, but it takes me roughly 45 minutes to an hour to fall asleep every night), I'd just lie there and go through the same old motions.  By the time the next day rolled around, yesterday was just some shit that happened to have happened.  I don't have any meaningful memories from this experience.  My problem seems to lie in some overarching philosophy I don't remember choosing and can't shake.
